A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gradient Aligned Regression via Pairwise Losses and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices sufficient for reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix B report original synthetic and real-world regression experiments, timing measurements, component ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains the original empirical results and adds batch-size experiments, prediction-moment convergence curves, standardized-data comparisons, and loss-specific timing measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same conventional MAE loss, two pairwise losses, KL-based robust aggregation, and mini-batch optimization procedure. New remarks explain existing components and their complementarity without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same two synthetic datasets and six real-world datasets covering eight benchmark tasks/settings. The new batch-size and standardization experiments reuse existing data and prediction targets.

E2.justification: The tabular and timing comparisons retain MAE, MSE, Huber, Focal (MAE), Focal (MSE), RankSim, RNC, and ConR. Synthetic comparators, PySR analyses, and AgeDB comparator exclusions also remain unchanged. The new standardized-data table uses the existing tabular comparator set.

E3.justification: V4 substantially extends evaluation settings with batch sizes 32–512 on Concrete Compressive Strength and both Parkinson targets, plus feature-and-label standardization across the five tabular datasets. Table 2 adds loss calculation/backpropagation time alongside whole-epoch time. Existing main benchmark splits, training budgets, and model configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices B.11–B.12 examine batch-size sensitivity, convergence of predicted means and standard deviations, and whether GAR's advantages persist after data standardization. These add substantive diagnostic and control experiments. Existing component ablations, backbone-depth analyses, and alpha sensitivity results are retained; Figure 7's new insets redisplay existing results.

E5.justification: The reported folds, seeds, repeated-run counts, mean/standard-deviation reporting, and Student's t-test practice are retained. New tables extend these reporting conventions to additional quantities and results; changed timing standard deviations do not establish a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the component-ablation results are unchanged, but Table 2 replaces timing values and adds loss-specific timings; GAR's Concrete Compressive Strength epoch time changes from 0.080 to 0.086 seconds. Tables 6–7 and Figure 12 add extensive batch-size, standardized-data, and convergence results. These concern additional experimental conditions, not revised accuracy under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical results, assumptions, aggregation derivations, and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged. Theorem 1 merely spells out the previously specified half-squared-error formula; the added standardization discussion introduces no new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about pairwise losses in label space, gradient alignment, linear computational complexity, and empirical effectiveness within the clean-data scope. The new experiments support the existing contribution without redefining it.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 now distinguishes comparable whole-epoch efficiency from somewhat greater loss-processing cost. Appendices B.11–B.12 add interpretations linking prediction-moment estimation to performance, recommend batch-size tuning, and distinguish dynamic mini-batch normalization from dataset standardization. The existing clean-data limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: New Table 4 discloses selected alpha values by tabular task, metric, and fold. Appendix B.8 newly specifies alpha=0.1 for AgeDB training from scratch and 1.0 for linear probing. These document existing experiments; the synthetic model and sampling details newly repeated in the main text were already in v3 Appendix B.3.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning relative to conventional regression, RankSim, RNC, ConR, and symbolic regression are unchanged. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized wording and explanation edits, relocates the clean-data scope statement, repeats synthetic settings in the main text, and expands Section 4.3 and Appendix B. The overall narrative structure and most prose remain intact. The copyright line also adds Tianbao Yang.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands with selected-alpha Table 4, batch-size Table 6, standardized-results Table 7, and six-panel Figure 12. Table 2 gains paired total-time/loss-time columns, and Figure 7 gains zoomed insets. The existing ablation table becomes Table 5, while Table 1's caption is corrected to describe its eight datasets/settings.

improvement.justification: V4 addresses practical gaps through batch-size and standardization controls, selected-alpha disclosures, and a timing breakdown that qualifies the efficiency interpretation. These improve reproducibility and understanding of GAR's behavior. The core theory and main accuracy results remain unchanged, and standardized-data advantages are not uniformly significant, making the overall quality gain useful but incremental.
